title: Hydration
log: 2026-10-29T12:14:26Z write: the API refused it in the chapter request, so it is written on its own next

draft.title: Hydration
card: Hydration is the body's water balance. During exercise, sweat is lost to cool the body, so water leaves faster than it is taken in.
Losing as little as 2% of body weight through sweat can lower performance. Skill, concentration and endurance can all drop, and the body finds it harder to control its temperature.
Before exercise, an athlete starts well hydrated. During exercise, they drink small amounts regularly to replace some of the sweat lost.
After exercise, they replace the fluid lost. Weighing before and after a session shows how much fluid was lost through sweat.
draft.remember: Even a small loss of body weight in sweat can hurt performance, so drink before, during and after exercise.

a.q: Why do athletes drink regularly during a long training session?
opts: To replace sweat lost, so performance is not lowered
To avoid needing to drink before the session starts
To stop the body from producing any sweat at all
To make up for fluid lost only after the session ends
a.why: Sweat is lost during exercise, and losing as little as 2% of body weight can lower performance. Drinking during the session replaces some of that loss. Drinking does not stop sweating, because sweat is how the body cools itself.
a.clue: Think about what is leaving the body while the athlete trains.

b.q: Priya weighs 60 kg before netball training and 58.5 kg after, with no drinks taken during the session. What does this show?
opts: She lost fluid and should drink to replace it afterwards
She lost 1% of her body weight, so she needs no extra fluid
She lost fat, so the change is not linked to hydration
She lost over 2% of her weight, so her sweat rate is normal
b.why: A drop of 1.5 kg in one session is mostly fluid lost through sweat, so she should replace it after exercise. It is about 2.5% of her body weight, which is above the 2% level that can lower performance. The idea that it was 1% is tempting but the sums do not support it.
b.clue: Work out 1.5 kg as a percentage of 60 kg.

a.best: To replace sweat lost, so performance is not lowered

b.best: She lost fluid and should drink to replace it afterwards

check.summary: No problems found. Both questions have one clearly right answer that the card supports, and 1.5 kg of 60 kg is correctly given as about 2.5% in the explanation.
